SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Fundamental Principles Four Faiths work) the , Non- stealing ,. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to learn the principles of Dharma?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the four selected fundamental Principles of Dharma for knowledge in the four faiths
2. practice the Principles of Dharma for spiritual nourishment
3. appreciate the Principles of Dharma for a balanced life

PART 1: Describe the four selected fundamental Principles of Dharma for knowledge in the four faiths

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the four selected fundamental Principles of Dharma for knowledge in the four faiths. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the four selected fundamental Principles of Dharma for knowledge in the four faiths.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Fundamental Principles Four Faiths work) the , Non- stealing ,” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the four selected fundamental Principles of Dharma for knowledge in the four faiths. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Practice the Principles of Dharma for spiritual nourishment

What this means
In this part you learn to practice the Principles of Dharma for spiritual nourishment. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practice the Principles of Dharma for spiritual nourishment.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practice the Principles of Dharma for spiritual nourishment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the Principles of Dharma for a balanced life

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the Principles of Dharma for a balanced life. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the Principles of Dharma for a balanced life.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the Principles of Dharma for a balanced life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Fundamental Principles Four Faiths work) the , Non- stealing , is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Fundamental Principles Four Faiths work) the , Non- stealing ,” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe the four selected fundamental Principles of Dharma for knowledge in the four faiths)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Fundamental Principles Four Faiths work) the , Non- stealing , in your own words. (skill: practice the Principles of Dharma for spiritual nourishment)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate the Principles of Dharma for a balanced life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Fundamental Principles Four Faiths work) the , Non- stealing , to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the four selected fundamental Principles of Dharma for knowledge in the four faiths.
3. Practise this skill: practice the Principles of Dharma for spiritual nourishment.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the Principles of Dharma for a balanced life.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Fundamental Principles Four Faiths work) the , Non- stealing , from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Fundamental Principles Four Faiths work) the , Non- stealing ,: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Fundamental Principles Four Faiths work) the , Non- stealing ,?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to learn the principles of Dharma?
2. How can the Principles of Dharma be practised in our daily lives?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Fundamental Principles Four Faiths work) the , Non- stealing , means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the four selected fundamental Principles of Dharma for knowledge in the four faiths.
5. Be able to: practice the Principles of Dharma for spiritual nourishment.
